# Template: piano_keys
A piano keyboard (one or two octaves) with any set of keys highlighted — chords, scales, intervals — plus letter names on the white keys and an optional caption. Highlights get their own ids in the order given, so a chord can be revealed note by note, each paired with a `play` command sounding that note. Choose this scene for ANY request about a piano or keyboard, chords or scales shown on keys, intervals (octave, fifth, third), semitones and black keys, or why notes sound good together. For a whole MELODY with sheet music AND pressed keys together, use note_sheet with keyboard: true instead.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "octaves": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "1 (C4-B4) or 2 (C3-B4, the default)."
  },
  "highlight": {
   "type": "array",
   "maxItems": 8,
   "items": {
    "type": "string"
   },
   "description": "Pitches to mark, e.g. [\"C4\", \"E4\", \"G4\"] — flats accepted (Db4 folds to C#4). Each gets its own id highlight_<i> in this order."
  },
  "labels": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Letter names on the white keys (default true)."
  },
  "caption": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Caption under the keyboard, e.g. \"C major = C + E + G\"."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- keys: the keyboard itself (white then black keys, a group)
- labels: the white-key letter names (a group, when labels)
- highlight_<i>: the mark on highlight[i] (draw them one at a time to build a chord)
- caption: the caption text, when set
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Show a C major chord on the piano." → params: {"highlight":["C4","E4","G4"],"caption":"C major = C + E + G","title":"The C major chord"}
Request: "Show an octave on the keyboard." → params: {"octaves":2,"highlight":["C3","C4"],"caption":"One octave apart: double the frequency","title":"The octave"}

In YAML: `template: piano_keys` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
